quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #8
										  					
  

40 Questions • Passing Score 32

questions.question: If cars keep passing you on both sides while you are in the center lane of an expressway, what should you do?

options.text: Stay in the center lane.
Move to the right lane.
Move to the left lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right lane.
questions.explanation: On roads with four or more lanes, drive in the right lanes unless you are passing or turning left. If you are driving slower than the traffic around you, use the right lane.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, when is it safe to move back into your lane?

options.text: When you cannot see the vehicle to your right.
When you see the vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.
When you have passed the vehicle's front bumper.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you see the vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Before moving back into your lane, make sure you are far enough ahead of the vehicle you passed. When you can see both of the vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror, you have enough space to return safely.

questions.question: To pass on a two-lane road, what should you do?

options.text: Sound your horn as you pass.
Flash your headlights as you pass.
Check the distance to any oncoming vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check the distance to any oncoming vehicles.
questions.explanation: Oncoming vehicles often seem slower than they really are. Make sure you have enough space to change lanes safely before passing. If you are not sure about an oncoming vehicle's speed, wait until it passes before you pass.

questions.question: How can you help keep the driver behind you a safe distance away?

options.text: Drive 10 mph faster than the car behind you.
Drive 10 mph slower than the car behind you.
Drive at a steady speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive at a steady speed.
questions.explanation: Drive at a steady speed and signal your turns and lane changes. This helps the driver behind you know what to expect and maintain a safe distance.

questions.question: Which one is a safe driving technique?

options.text: Using high beam lights in the fog.
Looking only straight ahead at the road.
Checking your rearview mirrors often.

questions.correctAnswerText: Checking your rearview mirrors often.
questions.explanation: Check your rearview mirrors every two to five seconds to stay aware of hazards. Do not stare straight ahead only. In fog, use low beam headlights, not high beam headlights.

questions.question: When driving in fog, what should you do?

options.text: Turn on your high beam headlights.
Slow down and use your low beam headlights.
Drive faster to avoid causing an accident.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and use your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: In fog, slow down and use low beam lights. If the fog is very thick and you cannot see, pull off the road and wait for it to clear.

questions.question: Traffic is merging into your lane on the freeway. What should you do?

options.text: Make room for them if you can.
Drive faster to protect your right-of-way.
Keep your position and do not move.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make room for them if you can.
questions.explanation: When traffic permits, make room to allow vehicles to merge into your lane safely.

questions.question: After passing a vehicle, when can you safely move back into the right lane?

options.text: After about three seconds.
When you cannot see the vehicle over your right shoulder.
When you can see the entire front of the vehicle in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see the entire front of the vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: You should see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror before returning to your lane. Always check your blind spots before moving back.

questions.question: How can you avoid skidding on slippery surfaces?

options.text: Shift to a lower gear after starting down a steep hill.
Speed up for curves and slow down to exit them.
Slow down before entering curves and intersections.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before entering curves and intersections.
questions.explanation: Slow down before entering a curve because you cannot see what is ahead. Braking during a curve may cause you to skid.

questions.question: Why should you signal continuously while turning?

options.text: It is illegal to turn off your signal before completing a turn.
It tells other drivers what you plan to do.
It is always unsafe to turn off a signal before completing a turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: It tells other drivers what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: Signal when turning, changing lanes, slowing down, or stopping so that other drivers, motorcyclists, bicyclists, and pedestrians know your intentions.

questions.question: When driving in work zones, what should you do?

options.text: Follow the driver in front of you closely.
Pass the driver in front of you as soon as you can.
Keep a safe distance from other vehicles and do not tailgate.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a safe distance from other vehicles and do not tailgate.
questions.explanation: In a work zone, keep a safe distance from barriers, trucks, equipment, workers, and other vehicles. Increase your following distance and avoid tailgating.

questions.question: What is the proper way to make a right turn?

options.text: Signal, slow down, and get into the left lane before turning.
Signal, slow down, and get into the right lane before turning.
Approach from the right lane, then move toward the middle of the street before turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, slow down, and get into the right lane before turning.
questions.explanation: Signal before you turn so other drivers know your plan. Slow down and stay close to the right curb as you approach the intersection.

questions.question: As you drive faster, what is important to do?

options.text: Turn on your headlights.
Look far ahead of your vehicle.
Change lanes frequently.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look far ahead of your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Your vehicle takes longer to stop as you speed up. Look far ahead to give yourself time to safely react to hazards.

questions.question: You are exiting the freeway on a curved ramp going downhill. What should you do?

options.text: Slow to a safe speed before the curve.
Slow to the posted freeway speed limit.
Wait until you are in the curve to begin braking.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow to a safe speed before the curve.
questions.explanation: Always slow down before entering a curve. You may not see hazards ahead, and braking in a curve may cause your vehicle to skid.

questions.question: At intersections, crosswalks, and railroad crossings, what should you always do?

options.text: Stop, listen, and proceed with caution.
Look to the sides of your vehicle to see what is coming.
Slowly pass vehicles that seem to be stopped for no reason.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look to the sides of your vehicle to see what is coming.
questions.explanation: At places where people may cross or traffic lines meet, look left and right to make sure no one is coming from the sides.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Sharp right turn ahead.
A road joins from the right.
The road will turn sharply right, then sharply left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road will turn sharply right, then sharply left.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. This sign warns you that the road will turn sharply right and then sharply left.

questions.question: What should you do when you approach an intersection with a flashing yellow light?

options.text: Stop before crossing.
Slow down and proceed with caution.
Wait for a green light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with caution.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down, check for cross traffic, and proceed carefully.

questions.question: When driving in fog, what lights should you use?

options.text: High beam headlights.
Parking lights.
Low beam headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog. High beams reflect back at you, making it harder to see.

questions.question: What often happens when you brake hard continuously on ice and snow?

options.text: You stop faster.
The front wheels lock, and you lose steering control.
The brakes stop from freezing.

questions.correctAnswerText: The front wheels lock, and you lose steering control.
questions.explanation: Hard braking on snow and ice can lock the front wheels and make steering impossible. Drive at a safe speed for conditions to avoid hard braking.

questions.question: How can you prevent hydroplaning in rainy weather?

options.text: Use cruise control to maintain constant speed.
Slow down.
Move to the road shoulder as soon as it rains.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Lower your speed in rain to prevent hydroplaning. Driving too fast can cause your tires to ride on water instead of the road, making your vehicle hard to control.

questions.question: A school bus ahead of you has red lights flashing. What should you do?

options.text: Stop and go when you think all children have left the bus.
Slow to 25 mph and pass carefully.
Stop and stay stopped while the red lights flash.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and stay stopped while the red lights flash.
questions.explanation: When a school bus has flashing red lights, you must stop and wait until the lights stop flashing. On a divided highway, you do not need to stop if the bus is on the opposite side.

questions.question: What does a yellow left arrow traffic signal mean?

options.text: Get ready to give way to oncoming traffic.
The protected left turn is ending.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: A yellow arrow tells you the protected left turn is ending. Get ready to yield to oncoming traffic. The yellow arrow warns you the green arrow is about to change.

questions.question: When are streets and highways most slippery?

options.text: When it has rained hard for several hours.
When they are clean and dry.
When rain first starts.

questions.correctAnswerText: When rain first starts.
questions.explanation: Roads are most slippery when rain first starts. Water mixes with oil and dirt on the road surface that has not washed away yet. Drive extra carefully during the first half hour of rainfall.

questions.question: On a slippery road, keep a following distance that is:

options.text: The same as normal.
Longer than normal.
Shorter than normal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Longer than normal.
questions.explanation: You need more distance to stop on a slippery road. Always keep a longer distance between your car and the car ahead on slippery roads.

questions.question: When should you give up your right-of-way?

options.text: Often, even at controlled intersections.
Whenever it helps prevent crashes.
Never. It confuses other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Whenever it helps prevent crashes.
questions.explanation: Do not assume other drivers will give you the right-of-way. Give up your right-of-way whenever it helps prevent crashes.

questions.question: You are on a one-way street. You may turn left onto another one-way street only if:

options.text: You speed up before turning.
Traffic moves to the right.
Traffic moves to the left.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moves to the left.
questions.explanation: You may turn left onto a one-way street where traffic moves to the left if there is no sign stopping you. You cannot turn left onto a one-way street where traffic moves to the right.

questions.question: Why is winter driving more dangerous than other seasons?

options.text: Ice, snow, freezing temperatures, and fog affect road conditions.
There are more hours of darkness.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Winter brings many dangers: ice, snow, rain, sleet, fog, and more darkness. Good drivers prepare for these bad conditions.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: You are about to enter a one-way street from the wrong direction.
U-turns are not allowed.
You may go if the way is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are about to enter a one-way street from the wrong direction.
questions.explanation: This sign marks a one-way road or entrance. If you see this sign, traffic is coming toward you. Turn around if you are driving toward it.

questions.question: You can drive off the road to pass another vehicle:

options.text: If the car ahead is turning left.
If there are two or more lanes in your direction.
Never.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: Never drive off the paved road or shoulder to pass another vehicle.

questions.question: Strong wind gusts on highways:

options.text: Only affect large vehicles.
Only cause visibility problems.
Can cause problems for all vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can cause problems for all vehicles.
questions.explanation: Strong wind can affect all drivers. It can reduce visibility by blowing dirt and dust, and it can physically push your vehicle sideways.

questions.question: When a railroad crossing gate is lowering, you should:

options.text: Speed up and cross before the gate closes.
Stop completely and wait.
Drive around the gate.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely and wait.
questions.explanation: You must stop at a railroad crossing when the gate is lowering. Do not try to go around it or cross.

questions.question: When you see this road sign, you should:

options.text: Keep right.
Keep left.
Pass with caution.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep right.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. This sign warns that a divided highway is starting. Stay in the right lane.

questions.question: Use your headlights on rainy, snowy, or foggy days:

options.text: To keep your engine warm.
So other drivers can see your vehicle.
To warn others about bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: So other drivers can see your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Headlights help other drivers see your vehicle in bad weather. If you need windshield wipers, you must use your low beam headlights.

questions.question: If your vehicle has a two-part safety belt, you should:

options.text: Use only the lap belt.
Use both the lap belt and shoulder belt.
Use only the shoulder belt.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the lap belt and shoulder belt.
questions.explanation: Wear both parts of your seat belt. Using only one part gives you less protection. If you have an automatic shoulder belt, always buckle your lap belt too.

questions.question: You must yield to an emergency vehicle using its siren and flashing lights by:

options.text: Driving to the right edge of the road and stopping.
Moving to the right lane and driving slowly until it passes.
Stopping right away, even if you are in an intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving to the right edge of the road and stopping.
questions.explanation: Move to the right edge of the road and stop for any emergency vehicle using its siren and lights. Do not stop in an intersection. Move again after it passes.

questions.question: At an intersection with a flashing yellow light, you must:

options.text: Stop completely.
Keep your normal speed.
Slow down and go with caution.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and go with caution.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means be alert and careful. Slow down and proceed with caution.

questions.question: At a red light with a green arrow, you may go in the direction of the arrow if:

options.text: You come to a complete stop first.
You wait for the light to change.
You are in the right lane and the way is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are in the right lane and the way is clear.
questions.explanation: If a green arrow appears in your lane, you may go in that direction when the way is clear. This is true whether the arrow appears alone or with another signal.

questions.question: Check your rearview mirrors:

options.text: Often to see traffic moving behind you.
To check if a vehicle is in your blind spot.
Only when you are slowing down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Often to see traffic moving behind you.
questions.explanation: Check your rearview mirrors frequently so you know where nearby vehicles are. Do not stare in one direction.

questions.question: This sign tells you that:

options.text: No turns are allowed.
The road narrows ahead.
There are curves ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: There are curves ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert you to upcoming conditions. This sign warns you about a winding road with curves ahead.

questions.question: To avoid glare from oncoming headlights:

options.text: Look briefly at the right side of the road.
Watch the centerline of the road.
Flash your high beams.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look briefly at the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: Look toward the right side of the road to avoid the bright lights of an oncoming car. Then look ahead to watch the other vehicle's position.
